expectations.prediction: At least 3 of 5 seeded defects (0.60) caught in their own turn. The five classes are lifted from the existing bench corpus precisely because they are already known-detectable there; a recall below 0.60 would therefore be a finding about the GATE (or about the panel), not about an unfair corpus. With n=5 the resolution is 0.20 per turn, so only a gross miss is interpretable.

Non-positive (<= 0) if the history-dependent layers help. HONEST PRE-COMMITMENT: this run will very likely NOT report a slope at all — it needs >= 5 turns with a defined FP burden, and a turn only has one if it produced findings AND the agent dispositioned them. 7 of 12 turns are clean and passing with zero findings is the DESIRED outcome, so n < 5 is the expected case, and `insufficient data (n=k)` is a successful run, not a failed one.
Median 1-2. Seeded turns are structurally >= 2 (block -> decision -> re-review) because the prompt DIRECTS the unsafe construction, so the agent rejects rather than fixes (spike finding S-6).
<= M3's miss rate, and never above it by construction: a defect missed in its own turn can still be flagged later.

Under $1 of OpenRouter spend for the whole run. NOTE: cost_usd is our own estimate from a single blended rate we choose (estimateCostUsd multiplies (input+output) by one number), NOT a billed amount. The key's usage is 0 at registration time, so the true spend will be read from OpenRouter afterwards and compared against M5.

Non-zero for at least one layer. If every layer is 0 the ablation has nothing to toggle and the counterfactual is vacuous for this run — which is itself a reportable outcome, not a reason to re-run until something appears.

known_limitations: n = 12 turns, 5 seeded. A single turn moves recall by 0.20. This pilot detects SIGNAL; it does not establish effect size.
ONE run. Any slope from it is a hypothesis, not a result; confirming it needs a second independent run.

The panel is deepseek-v3.2 (openrouter) + glm-5.2 (ollama), with codex absent because it is genuinely quota-exhausted until 2026-08-05T11:24:00.000Z. A different panel is a different system and the numbers do not transfer.
The ablation is an AGGREGATION-LAYER counterfactual over fixed reviewer output, not a behavioural A/B: it cannot re-drive the agent, because different verdicts would produce different diffs.
fp-ledger's ablation delta is an INTERVAL, not a point: the layer overwrites severity with INFO and the pre-suppression severity is persisted nowhere.
Agent turns are driven by `claude -p`, whose model and behaviour are outside this repo's control and are not pinned by this preregistration.
Anything that fails, times out or is skipped will be reported per-turn in the result's warnings[], including in the write-up.
